text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Syrian newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Syrian President Hafez al-Assad receives church patriarch.
- China says it stands by Syria for just peace.
- Israelis approve plan to build 132 homes in Arab Jerusalem.
- Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu reiterates stand on "security of Hebron settlers."

- Syrian Vice-President Abdul-Halim Khaddam says Syria insists on Israel's withdrawal from the Golan and south Lebanon and accuses Israel of blocking the peace process and turning the region back to the atmosphere of tension.
- Head of the political bureau in the PLO Farouk Kaddoumi calls on Arabs to boycott Israel.
- Syria's exports of cotton lint, onion and mineral waters were $8.2 million since the beginning of 1996.
- Syria's imports of raw and white sugar were $90.8 million this year.
- Capital of the Syrian textile companies totals 5.8 billion Syrian pounds.

- Ahead of the Arab-European partnership, expectations that the revenues of Syrian taxes and fees will drop by around 18 billion pounds. Suggestions to protect Syrian interests by listing Syrian imports and decreasing fees and exemptions and keeping the longest possible period of protection.
- People's Assembly (parliament) discuss measures to make up for inhabitants affected by the Tishreen dam.
